subject: Rooktide
prompt: A low river town on stepped terraces above a tidal landing at slack low water, so the barges sit in mud on their pilings and the channel is a thin bright line. Long, shallow-roofed sheds step up the bank; every building visibly has old salvaged plank sewn into newer timber, the joins unhidden and differently weathered. Thousands of rooks work the exposed flats, with part of the flock lifting at once. Palette rook-blue, tide-grey, new-thatch gold. Barge cranes and hull-change gear dominate the foreground. A rook-in-flight-over-a-rising-tideline emblem is painted on the largest shed's gable.
_note: Newly authored to the recovered block-in schema for this subject. Revised for task 6b: the original draft placed the mg shed terraces ABOVE (smaller y than) the bg tidal channel/mudflat — inverted depth. Fixed by moving the channel/mudflat to sit right at the horizon (0.58) and dropping the terraces' ground-contact below it, so the flat is glimpsed farthest-and-highest and the town reads as nearer, per the standard landscape convention. Also raised land coverage: terraces widened toward the frame edges, and a low barge-hull mass was added in the gap between the crane and the hull-change gear ('barges sit in mud on their pilings' is explicit in the brief) so the foreground band isn't half black. Composition unchanged in kind: tidal channel/mudflat on bg, stepped shed terraces climbing the bank on mg (asymmetric, denser on the left), barge cranes and hull-change gear as the dominant fg occluders per the brief's explicit 'dominate the foreground' instruction. Still authored, not measured.
